tasks.short: She watches signal lights and crossing traffic for hazards.

steps.what: Monitor lights indicating obstructions or other trains ahead
Look out and watch truck traffic at crossings to stay alert to potential hazards

tasks.design: She still monitors the lights ahead and still watches truck traffic at the crossing. Nothing in this task is written down, and no second person enters it. Written incident and delay reports for this occupation are other tasks.
tasks.previous_blocker: The obstruction and the crossing are in front of her, and the hazard is what she sees.
tasks.enabler_now: The automatable part named for this group is written incident, delay and shift reports, plus yard lists. This task is the watch itself, and that paperwork is a different task.
tasks.still_hard: A light that is wrong for the train ahead, and a truck that enters the crossing late.
tasks.human_edge: She is the person who can stop for what she sees.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still watches the lights and the crossing. She gains no right to pass a hazard.

reach.task: Read a signal aspect that protects the train ahead
reach.learn: Which aspect means she stops before the crossing

evidence.claim: She watches the lights and the crossing herself. Written incident and shift reports are a different task, so this watch stays.

assumptions: She watches the lights and the crossing herself. No second entry is part of this task.
Written incident, delay and shift reports are other tasks, so none of that time sits here.
Incremental upkeep is zero. No template, mapping, or list is added.
Of this task, the line watch is 58 and the crossing watch is 42.
unknowns: Whether a platform person already watches some crossings so she does not.
research_questions: Which crossings on this line still need her own look at the road?

already_counted.description: She still watches the lights ahead and the traffic at the crossing.

incremental.description: No template, mapping, or list is kept. Upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: She still watches the lights and the crossing. No step in this task is removed. The high stays at zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: She reports delays and emergencies to dispatch by radio.

steps.what: Report delays, mechanical problems and emergencies to supervisors or dispatchers using radios

tasks.design: She still reports delays, mechanical problems and emergencies to the dispatcher by radio, in her own words, at the moment they happen. No written report is part of this task.
tasks.previous_blocker: The dispatcher needs the train, the place and what is blocked, and only she has just seen it.
tasks.enabler_now: Written incident reports, shift summaries and regulator filings are other tasks. This task is the live radio call, and it stays.
tasks.still_hard: A radio that does not connect, and an emergency whose facts are still changing.
tasks.human_edge: She knows which problem blocks the train and which one can wait.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still makes the radio call. She gains no right to skip an emergency report.

reach.task: Pass a delay to the dispatcher
reach.learn: Which facts the first call needs: the train, the place, and what is blocked

evidence.claim: This task is the live radio call to a supervisor or dispatcher. A later written incident report is a different task.

assumptions: The radio call is the whole task. No second report entry is part of this statement.
Written incident reports and shift summaries are other tasks, so none of that time sits here.
Incremental upkeep is zero. No template, mapping, or list is added.
The call keeps its full share. Nothing in this task is removed.
unknowns: Whether a conductor already makes this radio call so she does not.
research_questions: Which facts does the first radio call have to include?

already_counted.description: She still makes the radio call about delays, mechanical problems and emergencies.

incremental.description: No template, mapping, or list is kept. Upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: She still speaks the radio call. No second entry is removed. The high stays at zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: She announces upcoming stops and schedule delays to passengers.

steps.what: Judge announcements to passengers about upcoming stops or schedule delays
Call the notifications of upcoming stops over the cab speaker
Speak a schedule delay the stop notification does not cover

tasks.design: She accepts the stop order for the run on the {OPS_SYSTEM}, and that acceptance is the version the cab may speak. When the train reaches the next stop on that order, the cab speaks that stop name instead of her call. She still speaks every schedule delay in her own words.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each upcoming stop was called by voice, even when the stop name and the train position were already known.
tasks.enabler_now: Once she has accepted the stop order, a position match can speak that stop name. Incident reports and shift summaries in this group are other tasks. A schedule delay still needs her voice, and this playback does not watch how she drives.
tasks.still_hard: Judging whether a schedule delay is real enough to tell passengers, and calling a stop the position has wrong.
tasks.human_edge: She decides which delay passengers hear. A spoken stop name does not explain a disruption.
tasks.altitude: Routine stop names can leave her voice. She still judges delays, and she gains no right to skip a hazard or an evacuation.

reach.task: Tell people on the platform what a delay means for the next train
reach.learn: Which delay wording tells passengers what to do, and which wording only repeats the stop name

evidence.claim: She already calls each upcoming stop by voice. A cab can speak that same stop name when the train position matches a stop on an order she has accepted.

assumptions: The work removed is the upcoming-stop call she already makes when the train reaches that stop. Schedule-delay speech stays hers.
She accepts the stop order for this run before any stop name is spoken. The fields are the next stop name on that order, and the train position.

Train position and the stop names on the run already sit in the {OPS_SYSTEM}. That feed is existing runtime, not new capture, and it is not a labour saving. The producer is the train running feed. If the position is missing, she calls the stop herself.
A changed stop order voids the earlier acceptance. The cab speaks only the order she has accepted for this run.
Incremental upkeep is zero. No template, mapping, or list is added. She does not keep a phrase list.
Of this task, judging which announcement is needed is 34, the upcoming-stop call she makes today is 38, and speaking a schedule delay is 28.
unknowns: Whether this cab already speaks stop names without her call.
Whether train position is already on the operations system for this line.
research_questions: On a normal run, how many stop calls are a fixed stop name, and how many are a delay she still has to explain?

already_counted.description: She still judges which announcement is needed and still speaks every schedule delay.

incremental.description: No phrase list is kept. Upkeep hours are zero.

approvals.approved_version: accepted stop order for this run

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low is zero when train position is missing and she still calls every stop, or when another role already speaks the stops. The high is 31 because she still calls a request stop or a stop the position has wrong, after no extra upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: She directs passengers through an emergency evacuation.

steps.what: Direct emergency evacuation procedures for the passengers on board

tasks.design: She still directs the evacuation from the doors she can see, and she still decides who moves and which door stays shut. No played message replaces that direction.
tasks.previous_blocker: The safe door depends on smoke, the crowd and what she can see from the cab.
tasks.enabler_now: Directing an evacuation is not covered by the paperwork prefill for incident and shift reports. Those reports are other tasks. This direction stays.
tasks.still_hard: A door that is blocked, and passengers who will not move until they see her.
tasks.human_edge: She chooses the exit from the car she is in, not from a general instruction.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still directs the evacuation. She gains no right to send people off without that direction.

reach.task: Decide which door opens first in an evacuation

evidence.claim: She directs the evacuation in person from what she can see. A written incident report after the event is a different task.

assumptions: Directing the evacuation stays full time. No step in this task is removed.
Incident and shift reports are other tasks, so none of that time sits here.
Incremental upkeep is zero. No template, mapping, or list is added.
The direction is the whole task. No checklist entry is part of this statement.
unknowns: Whether a passenger attendant already directs the car while she stays in the cab.
research_questions: Who decides which door opens first when both are on board?

already_counted.description: She still directs the evacuation from the doors she can see.

incremental.description: No template, mapping, or list is kept. Upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: She still directs the evacuation in person. No step is removed. The high stays at zero.

role.altitude: Only repeated stop-name calls can leave her voice. Watching the line, radio reports, delay announcements, and evacuations stay her week. She gains no right to leave a hazard or to send passengers off without directing them.
skills_to_grow: Accept a stop order before any stop name plays, and call the stop herself when the position is wrong.
Keep a radio report to the train, the place, and what is blocked.
Direct an evacuation from the doors she can see, not from a played message.
role.ambitious_version: She still watches the line, still radios delays and emergencies, and still directs an evacuation. A cab speaks only the next stop name she has already accepted for that run. She still tells passengers about a schedule delay in her own words. She does not gain a right to skip a hazard or an emergency call.
